paragraphs: ClearWorld sells solar systems that turn poles, new or already standing, into infrastructure for lighting, distributed energy, public safety, communications, and intelligent control. Cities and municipalities are one of the markets the site names for this equipment. Tribal, government, and institutional buyers are listed as well.

The patented design wraps solar vertically around a pole rather than using a flat panel, so the pole itself becomes a clean energy asset. Generating power at the pole is described as removing the need for costly grid extensions, trenching, and ongoing utility expenses. Poles already in the ground can be upgraded rather than replaced. The systems are meant to keep running off-grid during power outages. The solar hardware is paired with high-performance LED lighting.

ClearWorld traces its beginning to a patented idea in Louisiana. Remote area electrification is among the uses the site lists. Controls and real-time monitoring are described as optimizing how the installed systems perform. Literature offered for download includes a document on the RetroFlex systems.

quote.text: Patented vertical solar wrap technology that transforms any pole into a clean energy asset
